data.title: Dynamic reconfiguration of the functional brain network after musical training in young adults
data.text:
Title: Dynamic reconfiguration of the functional brain network after musical training in young adults

Nodes and edges of functional brain networks
The automated anatomical labeling (AAL) atlas was used to parcellate the whole brain into 90 regions, each representing a node of the functional brain network.

For each subject, the representative time series of each region was obtained by averaging the fMRI time series across all voxels within that region.

Functional connectivity matrices were constructed by computing Pearson correlation coefficients between the regional mean time series of all pairs of brain regions. Both positive and negative correlations were retained.

Fisher’s r-to-z transformation was applied to the correlation matrices to improve normality.

Graph theoretical analysis
Weighted undirected graphs were constructed. Network sparsity was controlled by applying a range of thresholds (0.10–0.34, step 0.01).

Global network measures including clustering coefficient, characteristic path length, global efficiency, local efficiency, and small-worldness were computed. The area under the curve (AUC) across sparsity thresholds was calculated for statistical analysis.
